scope: isolated actual TLS HTTP/1.1 on shared SATA SSD; synthetic data; fsync enabled; no concurrent builds/tests/profilers; production unchanged
trial_order: v1: per CPU 1/2/4 baseline-a,candidate-a,candidate-b,baseline-b; final: two per CPU 1/2/4 at 4g, then two per memory 1g/2g at 4CPU, baseline4CPU4g-c; sustained baseline4CPU2g then final2CPU2g and final4CPU2g; final mixed/crash; final4CPU4g200/s60s then final4CPU2g100/s60s
candidate_v1: CPU preparation parallelized; external capture callback serialized. Intermediate, not final.
final: standard read-only capture callback explicitly concurrent; credential metadata synchronized; unknown/custom callbacks remain serial by default

verification.targeted_race: parallel, postcapture, store, evidence, app, bootstrap, cmd/oimobbs; capture rejection/retry, both form modes, batch rebuild, callback contract, parallel eight-cap HTTP/recovery, cap/rate/backup/reclaim/recovery
verification.static: go vet; document and fixture checks

limitations: overload throughput is not a stable rate guarantee; skipped requests remain failures to supply planned load
shared-host storage variance prevents fixed speedup claims
one-board ordered preparation and three durability boundaries remain serial constraints
1g to 2g improves observed HTTP acceptance; 2g to 4g has no consistent throughput gain
SIGKILL is not power-loss or media-failure proof
full race suite, real browser UI, long archives, WAN/NIC and production rollout not verified in this change
